Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.24% today, capping a two-week rally of 13.2% that accelerated sharply from October 13 onward. The climb tracks closely with crude oil prices, which have climbed toward $109–$110 a barrel this week as geopolitical tensions escalated—Ukraine intensified drone strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, Iran signaled new military preparations, and tanker attacks disrupted Middle East shipping. For a major U.S. oil refiner, higher crude prices typically tighten margins in the short run, but the market appears to be betting that tighter global oil supply and sustained prices will support overall energy demand and refining economics.

The stock's sharp gain from $455 to $478 over two weeks suggests investors are viewing the geopolitical risk premium in oil as a structural support rather than a temporary spike. With U.S. diesel supply tight enough to draw attention to foreign refinery capacity and Trump ruling out nuclear escalation (which reduces tail-risk panic), the market may be settling into an expectation of elevated but stable crude and product prices—conditions that historically reward integrated refiners holding inventory and spare capacity.
